findings.title: Missing `key` prop on list items can cause React state leakage between rules
findings.body: In the `rules.map` call, the `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` is rendered without a `key` prop. This component contains stateful children (`RuleActionsButtons` with delete modal and silence drawer). Without a stable key, React may reuse component instances when the list changes (filtering, pagination, re-fetch), leading to state (e.g., an open delete confirmation) showing for the wrong rule or being lost. This is a regression from the previous version where `key={key}` was provided.

findings.title: Delete menu item won't appear for Grafana rules in list view
findings.body: The condition `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` requires `rulerRule` to be present. In the new list view, `rulerRule` is `undefined` because ruler API calls have been removed. Even though `canDelete` may be true based on `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the delete option will never render, preventing users from deleting Grafana managed rules from the list. The `handleDelete` callbacks no longer use `rulerRule`, so the condition should be changed to `canDelete && (...)`.

findings.title: Pause menu item won't appear for Grafana rules in list view
findings.body: The pause menu item is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, but in the list view `rulerRule` is undefined. Although `canPause` may be true from `grafanaPauseAbility`, the item is not rendered, making pause unavailable from the list. This is likely an oversight given the PR's goal to remove ruler dependencies from the list view; either the pause component needs to accept a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`, or the condition should be revisited.
